It is important to consider that the impurity yield is highly sensitive to the thermal energy applied to the system, the fluid processing speed which dictates the physical reaction time, the stoichiometric balance between the primary reagents, and the relative proportion of the reaction medium used. We need to optimize the reaction conditions of an N-benzylation reaction to minimize the formation of unwanted tertiary amine impurities. This optimization problem involves a 4-dimensional continuous search space consisting of specific controllable variables. It is important to consider that the impurity yield is highly sensitive to the thermal energy applied to the system, which can be controlled by the variable 'temperature' (typically evaluated within the bounds of 110.0 to 150.0 °C). It is also highly dependent on the fluid processing speed that dictates the physical reaction time, adjustable via the variable 'flow_rate' (expected to be around 0.2 to 0.4 mL/min). Furthermore, the outcome is strongly influenced by the stoichiometric balance between the primary reagents, specifically the variable 'ratio', the ratio of benzyl bromide equivalents to the methylbenzylamine reagent (generally ranging from 1.0 to 5.0), as well as the relative proportion of the reaction medium used, represented by the variable 'solvent', the solvent equivalents (such as 0.5 to 1.0 equivalents relative to the reagent stock solution). Please note that while these intervals provide a broad functional domain for each variable, they serve merely as reference boundaries; you can flexibly control the actual search space depending on your optimization strategy. The evaluation budget is {MAX_EVAL_VALUE}.
